name: Toast (web component)
summary: The toast as a framework-free element with an imperative toast() call: a short white pill that confirms an action, stacks in one bottom-right region, is announced to screen readers and leaves on its own.
highlights: toast.success('Slide saved') from any handler, no provider
Bottom-right stack, announced, focus never moved
Hover or focus pauses; Esc and ✕ dismiss; 0 = sticky
lead: ONE call, toast(), that renders an <aha-toast> into a shared <aha-toaster> region at the bottom-right of the window (Feedback C1). The pill matches the antd message themed by toast-theme.js value for value: white, radius 8, 9/12 padding, 14/22 ink text and a 16px status glyph in the default icon colour, never a status hue (C6). It exists for code that cannot reach antd's message: Vue 2 apps that only take <aha-*> elements, plain HTML pages, and React code outside the antd App context. The region owns two persistent live regions (polite, and assertive for an error), so every toast is read out without stealing focus; hovering or focusing the stack pauses every timer; Esc or the ✕ dismisses; a duration of 0 keeps it until dismissed and then shows the ✕.
codeNote: toast(content, options | duration) and toast.success / info / warning / error / loading(content, options | duration) return a handle { key, close(), update(patch), closed }. Options: { type, content, duration (seconds, default 3, 0 = sticky), key, closable, closeLabel, onClose }. A call with a key already on screen updates that toast in place and restarts its timer, which is how a loading toast turns into a success. toast.close(key) and toast.closeAll() dismiss. Content is text (never parsed as HTML) or a Node. The first call appends one <aha-toaster> to <body>; mount your own near the app root to move it (--aha-toaster-offset-x / -y) or to cap the stack (max, default 5).

spec.label: Pill
spec.value: white (bg-elevated), radius 8, padding 9 12, width fits the text up to 384 (never wider than the viewport less 32), the antd message shadow

spec.label: Text
spec.value: 14/22 ink, wraps; text only, a Node for rich content

spec.label: Glyph
spec.value: 16px stroke status icon in icon-default (success check-circle, info, warning-circle, error x-circle); loading shows the small aha-spin; never a status hue (Feedback C6)

spec.label: Dismiss
spec.value: the shared ✕ (tertiary icon-only xs aha-button, system-x 16) pinned to the first line; shown only when duration is 0 or `closable` is set

spec.label: Region
spec.value: <aha-toaster>: fixed 24 from the right and bottom (16 under 576px), z-index 2010, newest at the bottom, 8 between items, max 5 (the oldest leaves first); role region named "Notifications"

spec.label: Motion
spec.value: rises 12 and fades in over 0.3s; leaves by fading and collapsing its height so the stack closes up; prefers-reduced-motion switches both off

spec.label: Behaviour
spec.value: announced through the region's persistent live region (polite; assertive for an error); never takes focus; hover or focus anywhere in the stack pauses every timer and they resume with the time left; Esc on a focused toast dismisses it and focus goes back to where it was before the stack

props.name: toast(content, options)
props.desc: Opens a toast; options may be a number (duration). Returns { key, close(), update(patch), closed }

props.name: toast.close(key) / closeAll()
props.desc: Dismisses one toast or every toast in the region

props.name: type
props.desc: The glyph; error is announced assertively. No type, no glyph

props.name: duration
props.desc: Seconds on screen; 0 keeps it until dismissed

props.name: closable
props.desc: Shows the ✕ on a timed toast

props.name: max
props.desc: On <aha-toaster>: the most items on screen; the oldest leaves when one more arrives

props.name: --aha-toaster-offset-x / -y
props.desc: On <aha-toaster>: distance from the right and bottom edges (16px under 576px)

props.name: close
props.desc: Cancelable, composed. detail.source is timeout, close-button, escape, overflow or method

props.name: closed
props.desc: Composed. The toast has left; the handle's closed promise resolves

whenToUse.when: a short confirmation of something the user just did (saved, copied, sent), from code that cannot reach antd's message: Vue 2, plain HTML, React outside the antd App
a React or Vue 3 app that already themes antd with toast-theme.js
the message needs a title, a sentence of detail or one action such as Undo
the message must stay on the page next to what it is about

opinion.note: Keep it to one short line in sentence case with no full stop. Never put the only way to do something in a toast: it leaves on its own. An error the user must act on is sticky (duration 0) or an inline Alert. A retryable error is type warning with a calm "Try again"; type error is for a failure trying again can't fix (ux-writing C5).
